title: Pilot sync — version guardrails & fallback routing
summary: Weekly POC sync to review model selection results from last 48h, validate pinned version behavior, and agree on fallback/rollback playbook. SE ran a latency/cost matrix and a small replay; customer raised questions about KV cache consistency and audit logs for compliance. Agreed to run a 24h traffic replay with canary routing + runbook for automatic soft-fallback after 3% quality regressions.
topics: audit logs and KMS for Private deployment
next_steps: Redwood to share 48h benchmark spreadsheet and raw traces (link) by 2025-10-30
Customer to provide sample traffic slice and success criteria for quality by 2025-11-03
Schedule security deep-dive (SOC2/KMS) w/ security team week of 2025-11-10
Run 24h replay with canary (10% traffic) starting 2025-11-05
action_items: Samira: upload benchmark spreadsheet + short README to customer Drive by 2025-10-30
Diego: prepare canary routing config example and rollback script snippets by 2025-11-04
Maya: share labeled quality eval set (500 prompts) by 2025-11-03
Ellen: confirm network egress constraints and whether private VPC required by 2025-11-07
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly pilot sync for ParcelFlow, we're gonna go over the last 48 hours of runs and talk model pinning and fallback.
[00:14] Roberto: great, thanks Samira. quick heads up, we had a spike on our side on thursday, so some of the traces are a little noisy.
[00:26] Diego Ramos: mm-hmm, noted — the SE run does account for irregular bursts but yeah some of the tail latencies came from long prompt sequences, so we annotated those.
[00:40] Maya Chen: can you remind me which models we compared in the matrix? I saw redwood-2 and a quantized variant but not sure on the exact tags.
[00:52] Samira Patel: sure, we tested rwd-2-base:2025-10-15 (float32), rwd-2-q4_0:2025-10-18 (quantized), and rwd-2-slim:2025-09-30 (faster smaller). Diego, you wanna say quick summary?
[01:05] Diego Ramos: yeah, so the float32 had best quality by eval scores — roughly +2.5% higher on your labeled set — but median latency was 210ms. Quantized q4_0 dropped median latency to 125ms and cost per 1M tokens was about 38% lower. Slim variant was low cost but regressed on entity-extraction and hallucination checks.
[01:34] Roberto: okay so our priority is extraction accuracy — hallucinations kill downstream billing reconciliations — but cost is also obviously important. what do you recommend for pinning?
[01:47] Diego Ramos: for production if extraction is primary I'd recommend pinning to rwd-2-base for the main route and using a soft-fallback to rwd-2-q4_0 when latency SLOs are violated or Dedicated capacity is exhausted. soft-fallback means keep the request semantics and downstream tracing the same, but you do allow a small quality delta during peak times.
[02:09] Maya Chen: mhm. how do you detect the quality delta automatically? that's where we worry — we can't manually check every minute.
[02:21] Diego Ramos: good point; common pattern is to run a shadowor sampling approach — keep 2% of traffic mirrored to the candidate model and compute lightweight heuristics (entity match rate, token overlap). if your regression crosses threshold (say 3% entity misses) we trigger automatic rollback. note this needs the metric definitions from you.
[02:48] Maya Chen: ok we'll provide the labeled set. How about KV cache concerns? we saw some inconsistent completions when we did session-affine tests.
[02:59] Samira Patel: I think that's the KV cache mismatch — sometimes when switching between pinned versions and a fallback, the cache keys aren't compatible and you can get a warm vs cold behavior. Diego — do we have an approach?
[03:14] Diego Ramos: yes, two approaches: prefix-agnostic cache keys so both variants read same entries, or flush-on-rollover which causes a small latency blip but consistent outputs. For your workflows which are session long, I'd recommend prefix-agnostic keys + cache version tag in telemetry so you can debug. we documented a snippet in the playbook.
[03:35] Ellen Park: flushing on rollover sounds scary for tail latency — we need SLOs.
[03:40] Diego Ramos: agreed, that's why prefix-agnostic is safer. slight risk of stale cached embeddings when model paramization differs, but in practice with the two model variants we ran it's low.
[03:55] Roberto: what about audit logs, we need full tracing for compliance — every prompt+response and model version id.
[04:03] Samira Patel: Redwood's Private and Dedicated options can persist per-request audit logs, including model ID, commit hash, and KV-cache tags. For Private we integrate with KMS/HSM and you get retention options. We'll share the security pack in a moment.
[04:20] Maya Chen: perfect. also how do rollbacks look operationally — automatic vs manual? we want an initial manual verification step.
[04:30] Diego Ramos: recommended flow: 1) canary at 10% traffic for 24 hours with mirrored telemetry; 2) auto-alert if quality drops >3% or latency >2x baseline; 3) if alert fires, automatic soft-fallback engages and an Ops ticket is created; 4) manual audit for hard rollback. This gives quick mitigation but human-in-loop for full rollback.
[04:59] Samira Patel: linking that to your runbook — we can wire PagerDuty alerts and create a Slack channel for canary ops.
[05:10] Roberto: good. can we see the 48h numbers now?
[05:15] Diego Ramos: yes pulled up the sheet — [link redacted in transcript] — key items: overall token throughput ~1.2M tokens/day, 95th latency for base model 480ms, quantized 220ms. error rate (time outs/rejects) was 0.3% for both. Quality eval on your sample: base 92.4 F1, q4_0 89.9 F1, slim 81.2 F1.
[05:42] Maya Chen: 2.5 point delta is ok if cost savings 38% — what's the operational cost implication for us?
[05:51] Samira Patel: we modeled cost per 1M tokens — base ~$120, q4_0 ~$74, slim ~$42 (these are rough hosted numbers). If you move to Dedicated the unit cost goes down depending on reserved hours and GPU type — we can produce a dedicated quote.
[06:12] Roberto: that's helpful. timeline-wise, we want to move to pilot in-prod in early december. what's needed from Redwood for that?
[06:22] Samira Patel: to hit that timeline: 1) final quality gates defined by you by Nov 3, 2) 24h replay with canary by Nov 5-6, 3) security review and contract for Dedicated/Private by Nov 14, 4) pilot signoff week of Dec 1.
[06:40] Maya Chen: ok we'll try to meet those.
[06:43] Diego Ramos: a couple of gotchas in your traces — we saw some prompts that include trailing JSON that caused tokenization mismatch between model variants; when switching models the token alignments change and entity extraction drops. We recommend normalizing inputs (strip trailing meta) before sending.
[07:02] Roberto: noted, we'll add a normalization layer.
[07:07] Ellen Park: about fallback routing — is it possible to route by tenant? some of our big customers need guaranteed accuracy and cannot see soft-fallbacks.
[07:17] Diego Ramos: yes, Redwood routing policies support per-tenant routes. You can pin high tier tenants to base always, while lower tier tenants get fallback. You configure this in the route table and the console.
[07:29] Maya Chen: good. what about SSO and audit — we will need SAML and role-based access.
[07:35] Samira Patel: that's supported — SAML, SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC, and audit trails. For Private deployments we can integrate into your IdP. We'll attach the security architecture doc.
[07:48] Roberto: any competitor considerations we should be aware of? we ran a quick bench vs Anthropic and OpenAI in-house but those are different price points.
[07:56] Samira Patel: yeah, Anthropic showed similar quality on few-shot tasks but cost profile differs; OpenAI endpoints had lower latencies in some regions — we can show region-specific latencies if that's relevant.
[08:09] Maya Chen: ok. next — runbook for rollback — can you summarize recommended thresholds again?
[08:15] Diego Ramos: threshold suggestions: quality regression >3% entity-f1 over mirrored 2% sample OR absolute latency 95th > 2x baseline OR error rate >0.8% sustained for 5 minutes. On threshold breach: auto-soft-fallback, create incident, pages on-call. Manual human review decision point at T+30 minutes.
[08:42] Roberto: what constitutes soft-fallback in logs? do we capture which requests hit fallback?
[08:48] Diego Ramos: yes all requests record model_id, route, and a fallback boolean in trace. You get rollup metrics and per-request traces for debugging.
[08:58] Maya Chen: I noticed some transcription lookback issues in the SDK demos — is there any SDK version that causes KV key naming differences?
[09:07] Diego Ramos: ah, yes older SDKs used an inline keyprefix which caused mismatch; new SDK 1.8.3 removes prefixing by default. If you're on older SDK we can give a migration patch.
[09:20] Samira Patel: I'll add that to the action items.
[09:24] Roberto: timeline check — you mentioned dedicated quote — can we get a rough estimate?
[09:28] Samira Patel: rough estimate for dedicated GPU pool sized for your 1.2M tokens/day footprint with headroom is $18k–$25k/month depending on commitment and GPU class. We'll follow up with exact pricing.
[09:42] Maya Chen: good. One more thing — in the previous run the soft-fallback caused a 5% total-variance in output length which broke downstream parsers. Any guidance?
[09:53] Diego Ramos: that sounds like temperature or stop-token differences between variants. We recommend fixing decoding config at the route layer (explicit temperature, top_p, stop tokens) so both variants receive same decoding opts.
[10:08] Roberto: makes sense.
[10:10] Samira Patel: any other open questions?
[10:13] Zack Li: quick note — we'll anonymize PII in the sample traffic before sharing. timeline still ok.
[10:18] Maya Chen: yes we'll aim for Nov 3 for the eval set.
[10:22] Samira Patel: great. to recap: Redwood shares benchmark + traces by Oct 30, customer provides labeled eval by Nov 3, Redwood prepares canary config and rollback scripts by Nov 4, run 24h canary Nov 5. Security deep dive to be scheduled week of Nov 10.
[10:40] Roberto: agreed.
[10:42] Ellen Park: one operational ops question — if we do Private deployment, what's the KMS workflow? who holds keys?
[10:50] Samira Patel: for Private you can bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) or use Redwood-managed keys; BYOK gives you full control and key rotation policies. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[11:02] Diego Ramos: i'll also include a short playbook for prefix-agnostic cache keys and a sample terraform snippet for routing rules.
[11:10] Maya Chen: thanks Diego.
[11:12] Samira Patel: ok last bit — are we comfortable with the automatic soft-fallback logic as the mitigation step?
[11:19] Roberto: yes as long as tenants can be excluded and we have clear alerts.
[11:24] Maya Chen: yes.
[11:26] Samira Patel: perfect. i'll send the notes and action items. thanks everyone.
[11:31] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" for KV cache), some proper nouns may be off. Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link redacted), security pack (link redacted), sample canary config (attached in follow-up).
